plans.title: CDC propagation of a new `class` entity from publisher to consumer, validated against the ODCS v3.1.0 contract

setup.description: Ensure the publisher service is running and reachable, with CDC pipeline active and connected to the consumer service.
Ensure the consumer service is running and reachable at its live API target /me/classes.
Confirm the ODCS v3.1.0 JSON schema is available for contract validation.
Ensure no pre-existing class record with the test sourcedId exists on either publisher or consumer to avoid state collisions.
Confirm the CDC lag/propagation window is known and a suitable wait period is configured before consumer assertions are made.

trigger.payloadShape: JSON object containing all required fields: sourcedId (string), status (string), dateLastModified (date), title (string), classType (string), course (object), school (object), terms (non-empty array); optionally includes classCode (string), grades (array), location (string), metadata (object), subjects (array)

propagation.waitFor: CDC pipeline delivers the new class record from publisher to consumer

assertions.assertion: The POST response status is 2xx, confirming the class entity was accepted and persisted by the publisher.
The response body includes the created class record with all submitted required fields (sourcedId, status, dateLastModified, title, classType, course, school, terms) matching the submitted values.
After CDC propagation, a GET to /me/classes returns a 2xx response and the 'items' array contains an entry whose sourcedId matches the one created on the publisher.

The matching class record in 'items' contains all required ODCS contract fields: sourcedId (string), status (string), dateLastModified (date), title (string), classType (string), course (object), school (object), terms (array).

Each required field in the propagated class record is non-null and conforms to its declared ODCS v3.1.0 type: sourcedId and status and title and classType are strings; dateLastModified is a valid date; course and school are objects; terms is a non-empty array.

Optional fields present in the publisher payload (classCode, grades, location, metadata, subjects) are also present in the consumer record and match their published values, confirming full contract mirroring of the producer's shape.

The full class record as received at /me/classes (items entry) validates without errors against the official ODCS v3.1.0 JSON schema, confirming the consumer contract is structurally equivalent to the producer's org contract shape.

plans.title: CDC propagation of class entity validates ODCS enum data-quality rules on consumer (classType ∈ {homeroom, scheduled}, status ∈ {active, tobedeleted})

setup.description: Ensure the publisher service is running and has write access to the class entity endpoint.
Ensure the consumer service is running and its /me/classes endpoint is accessible.
Ensure the CDC pipeline between publisher and consumer is active and operational.
Ensure no pre-existing class record with the test sourcedId exists on either service; clean up if necessary.
Confirm the ODCS contract for class is loaded on the consumer, including data-quality rules: classType ∈ {homeroom, scheduled} and status ∈ {active, tobedeleted}.

trigger.payloadShape: Object containing all required class fields: sourcedId (unique string), status (one of: active, tobedeleted), dateLastModified (ISO date string), title (non-empty string), classType (one of: homeroom, scheduled), course (object with at minimum a sourcedId reference), school (object with at minimum a sourcedId reference), terms (non-empty array of term references). Optional fields may include classCode, grades, location, metadata, subjects.

propagation.waitFor: The newly created class record appears in the consumer's /me/classes response under the 'items' array, identified by the matching sourcedId.

assertions.assertion: GET /me/classes returns HTTP 200 and the response body contains an 'items' array.
The 'items' array contains exactly one record whose 'sourcedId' matches the sourcedId submitted by the publisher in the trigger.
The propagated class record's 'classType' field is present and its value is one of the ODCS-allowed enum values: 'homeroom' or 'scheduled'. Any other value constitutes a data-quality rule violation.
The propagated class record's 'status' field is present and its value is one of the ODCS-allowed enum values: 'active' or 'tobedeleted'. Any other value constitutes a data-quality rule violation.
The propagated class record's 'classType' value exactly matches the value supplied by the publisher in the trigger payload (no transformation or truncation occurred in transit).
The propagated class record's 'status' value exactly matches the value supplied by the publisher in the trigger payload (no transformation or truncation occurred in transit).
All other required fields (sourcedId, dateLastModified, title, course, school, terms) are present and non-null on the propagated record, confirming full contract fidelity beyond the enum fields.

plans.title: CDC propagation of org entity from publisher to consumer, validating OneRoster v1.2 Org field mapping

setup.description: Ensure the publisher service is running and accessible at its /orgs endpoint.
Ensure the consumer service is running and its CDC listener is active and subscribed to org change events from the publisher.
Ensure no pre-existing org record with the test sourcedId exists in either service to avoid collision.
Confirm CDC pipeline (e.g., Debezium, Kafka, or equivalent) is healthy and able to relay org events from publisher to consumer.

trigger.payloadShape: A JSON object representing a OneRoster v1.2 Org with all required fields: sourcedId (unique string), status (string, e.g. 'active'), dateLastModified (ISO 8601 date string), name (string), type (string, e.g. 'school'); and optional fields: identifier (string), metadata (object with arbitrary key-value pairs), parent (object with at minimum a sourcedId reference), children (array of org reference objects).

propagation.waitFor: Consumer service reflects the newly created org record, identifiable by the same sourcedId written to the publisher.

assertions.assertion: The POST /orgs response returns a 2xx status code, confirming the org was accepted and persisted by the publisher.

The org record retrievable from the publisher (via GET /orgs or equivalent) contains exactly the fields: sourcedId, status, dateLastModified, metadata, name, type, identifier, parent, and children — matching the OneRoster v1.2 Org schema defined in §3.1.
The required fields sourcedId, status, dateLastModified, name, and type are present and non-null in the persisted org record on the publisher.
After CDC propagation, the consumer contains an org record whose sourcedId matches the one written to the publisher.

The org record on the consumer contains all nine OneRoster v1.2 Org fields: sourcedId, status, dateLastModified, metadata, name, type, identifier, parent, and children — no fields are dropped or renamed during CDC transit.
The required fields sourcedId, status, dateLastModified, name, and type are present, non-null, and their values exactly match those originally submitted to the publisher.
The children field on the consumer-side org record is of array type, matching the contract schema definition.
The metadata field on the consumer-side org record is of object type, matching the contract schema definition.
The parent field on the consumer-side org record is of object type, matching the contract schema definition.
The dateLastModified field on the consumer-side org record is a valid ISO 8601 date string, consistent with the contract schema's date type.

plans.title: R-06: sourcedId declared as unique primary key of the org object — CDC propagation from publisher to consumer

setup.description: Ensure the publisher service is running and reachable at its live API base URL with access to the /orgs endpoint.
Ensure the consumer service is running and connected to the CDC pipeline that receives org change events from the publisher.
Ensure no pre-existing org record shares the sourcedId value chosen for this test, guaranteeing uniqueness preconditions are clean.
Confirm CDC infrastructure (e.g. event bus / outbox) is active and capable of propagating org write events from publisher to consumer.

trigger.payloadShape: A JSON object representing a new org with all required fields: sourcedId (a unique string acting as primary key), name (string), status (string), type (string), and dateLastModified (date). Optional fields such as identifier, metadata, parent, and children may be omitted.

propagation.waitFor: Consumer service has received and processed the CDC event for the newly created org identified by the posted sourcedId.

assertions.assertion: The POST /orgs response returns a success status code (2xx), confirming the org was created.
The created org record returned by the publisher contains a sourcedId field whose value exactly matches the sourcedId provided in the request payload, confirming it is stored as the primary key.
A second POST to /orgs with the same sourcedId value must be rejected (non-2xx, e.g. 409 Conflict), confirming sourcedId uniqueness is enforced at the publisher.
After CDC propagation, the consumer holds an org record whose sourcedId matches the one posted to the publisher, confirming the primary key is preserved end-to-end.
The org record on the consumer side contains all required fields (sourcedId, name, status, type, dateLastModified) with values identical to those sent in the original publisher POST payload.
No duplicate org records with the same sourcedId exist on the consumer, confirming that sourcedId uniqueness semantics are upheld across the CDC boundary.

plans.title: CDC propagation: publisher emits class event on `class-events` topic → consumer ingester parses envelope and validates class data against ODCS schema

setup.description: Ensure the `class-events` SNS topic is active and the subscriber Lambda is deployed and wired to the consumer ingestion pipeline.
Ensure the consumer service is running and its `/me/classes` endpoint is reachable.

Prepare a valid class payload satisfying all required ODCS fields: classType, course (object), dateLastModified (date), school (object), sourcedId (string), status (string), terms (array), and title (string).
Record any pre-existing class records on the consumer via GET /me/classes so that the new record can be distinguished after propagation.

trigger.payloadShape: An SNS-envelope-wrapped class object containing all required ODCS fields: sourcedId (string), status (string), title (string), classType (string), course (object), school (object), terms (array), dateLastModified (date); optionally including classCode (string), grades (array), location (string), metadata (object), subjects (array).

propagation.waitFor: Subscriber Lambda on `class-events` topic completes invocation and the consumer store reflects the ingested record

assertions.assertion: After CDC propagation, GET /me/classes returns a response whose `items` array contains a record matching the sourcedId published by the publisher.
The ingested class record in `items` has a non-null `classType` field matching the value supplied in the published payload.
The ingested class record in `items` has a `course` field of type object, matching the value supplied in the published payload.
The ingested class record in `items` has a `dateLastModified` field that is a valid date value matching the value supplied in the published payload.
The ingested class record in `items` has a `school` field of type object, matching the value supplied in the published payload.
The ingested class record in `items` has a `status` field matching the value supplied in the published payload.
The ingested class record in `items` has a `terms` field of type array, matching the value supplied in the published payload.
The ingested class record in `items` has a `title` field matching the value supplied in the published payload.

If optional fields (classCode, grades, location, metadata, subjects) were included in the published payload, confirm they appear with correct types (string, array, string, object, array respectively) in the ingested record in `items`.
No schema-validation error is logged or surfaced by the ingester Lambda for the delivered class message; the record is stored without rejection.

plans.title: Cross-service CDC propagation of POST /orgs upsert (create and overwrite) validated against ODCS org schema

setup.description: Ensure no org with the test sourcedId (e.g. 'test-org-001') exists on the publisher or consumer before the test begins; delete or confirm absence via the publisher's GET /orgs endpoint filtering by sourcedId.
Record the current item count at publisher GET /orgs to use as a baseline for assertions.
Confirm the CDC pipeline between publisher and consumer is active and healthy, with known maximum propagation latency.

trigger.payloadShape: JSON object containing all required ODCS org fields: sourcedId (string, unique test value), status (string), dateLastModified (date string), name (string), type (string); optionally including identifier (string), metadata (object), parent (object), children (array)

propagation.waitFor: CDC pipeline delivers the upserted org record from publisher to consumer; poll or await event confirmation up to the maximum known propagation latency

assertions.assertion: The POST /orgs response status is 201 Created when the sourcedId did not previously exist, confirming a new org was created.
The response body from POST /orgs includes the org record with all submitted fields (sourcedId, status, dateLastModified, name, type) matching the request payload exactly.
GET /orgs on the publisher returns the newly created org in the 'items' array, with all required fields (sourcedId, status, dateLastModified, name, type) matching the posted values.
After CDC propagation, the consumer's store contains an org record whose sourcedId matches the one posted to the publisher.
The org record on the consumer has name, type, status, and dateLastModified values identical to those submitted in the POST /orgs request payload.
A second POST /orgs with the same sourcedId but updated field values (e.g. a new name and dateLastModified) returns 200 OK, confirming the overwrite/upsert path was taken.
After the overwrite POST, GET /orgs on the publisher returns exactly one org record for that sourcedId (no duplicate), and its fields reflect the updated values from the second POST.

After CDC propagation of the overwrite event, the consumer's org record for the same sourcedId is updated to reflect the new field values from the second POST, with no duplicate records for that sourcedId.

plans.title: R-15: GET /orgs/{sourcedId} returns 200 OK with org representation, propagated via CDC to consumer

setup.description: Ensure at least one org record exists on the publisher service by creating or confirming an org with known sourcedId, name, status, type, and dateLastModified fields populated to satisfy the contract schema required fields.
Record the sourcedId of the pre-existing or newly created org to be used in the trigger and assertions.
Confirm the CDC pipeline between publisher and consumer is active and healthy before running the test.

trigger.payloadShape: Object containing required fields: sourcedId (string), name (string), status (string), type (string), dateLastModified (date); optional fields: identifier (string), metadata (object), parent (object), children (array)

propagation.waitFor: Consumer has received and persisted the org record identified by the known sourcedId

assertions.assertion: After the write, GET /orgs/{sourcedId} on the publisher returns HTTP 200 OK.
The response body contains an org object whose sourcedId matches the known sourcedId used in the trigger.
The response body org object includes all required fields: sourcedId, name, status, type, and dateLastModified, each with a non-null value matching what was written.

The response body structure is consistent with the contract schema: children is an array (if present), metadata is an object (if present), parent is an object (if present), and identifier is a string (if present).
After CDC propagation, the consumer's store contains an org record with the same sourcedId as written to the publisher.
The consumer's org record has name, status, type, and dateLastModified values that exactly match those written by the publisher.
Optional fields (identifier, metadata, parent, children) on the consumer's org record, if present, match the corresponding values from the publisher's written payload.

plans.title: CDC propagation of a newly created org from publisher to consumer, verified against paginated GET /orgs

setup.description: Ensure the publisher service is running and reachable at its live API target /orgs.
Ensure the consumer service is running and subscribed to CDC events for the org entity.
Ensure the CDC pipeline (e.g. Debezium or equivalent) is active and routing org change events from publisher to consumer.
Record the current count of orgs on both publisher and consumer to establish a baseline for assertions.

trigger.payloadShape: Object containing all required org fields: sourcedId (string), status (string), dateLastModified (date), name (string), type (string); optionally including identifier (string), children (array), parent (object), and metadata (object).

propagation.waitFor: Consumer service reflects the newly created org in its own data store, as confirmed by the org's sourcedId being present in the consumer's org list.

assertions.assertion: After POST /orgs, the publisher responds with a success status and the created org is retrievable via GET /orgs, appearing in the paginated response body under the 'items' array with the correct sourcedId, name, status, type, and dateLastModified matching the posted payload.

GET /orgs on the publisher returns HTTP 200 OK with a paginated structure: the response includes an 'items' array and pagination metadata (e.g. totalCount or equivalent per OQ-4), and the newly created org is present in the appropriate page.
After CDC propagation, GET /orgs on the consumer returns HTTP 200 OK and the 'items' array contains the newly created org identified by its sourcedId.

The org record on the consumer contains all required fields — sourcedId, status, dateLastModified, name, type — with values that exactly match those posted to the publisher, confirming faithful CDC propagation.
Optional fields included in the POST payload (identifier, children, parent, metadata) are also present and match on the consumer side, with no data loss during CDC propagation.

plans.title: Org type-filtered query propagates via CDC and returns only matching orgs; invalid type returns 400

setup.description: Ensure at least two orgs of distinct types exist in the publisher's DynamoDB table — e.g., one org with type='district' (orgA) and one with type='school' (orgB) — each with all required fields (sourcedId, status, name, type, dateLastModified) populated and confirmed present via the publisher's /orgs endpoint.
Confirm the DynamoDB GSI keyed on 'type' is active and in ACTIVE status before the test run begins.
Confirm the consumer service is subscribed to CDC events from the publisher's org table and that its local org store is in sync (i.e., both orgA and orgB are visible on the consumer side).

trigger.payloadShape: Object containing required org fields: sourcedId (string), status (string), name (string), type (string, valid enum value e.g. 'department'), dateLastModified (date); optionally: identifier (string), metadata (object), parent (object), children (array)

propagation.waitFor: CDC event for the newly created org (type='department') is consumed and the record is visible on the consumer side

assertions.assertion: POST /orgs with a valid org payload (type='department') returns HTTP 201 (or 200), and the response body includes the newly created org's sourcedId and type='department'.

GET /orgs?type=department returns HTTP 200, and the response body 'items' array contains only orgs whose type field equals 'department', including the newly created org; no orgs of type 'district' or 'school' appear in 'items'.
GET /orgs?type=district returns HTTP 200, and the response body 'items' array contains only orgA (type='district'); the newly created org (type='department') does not appear.
GET /orgs?type=INVALID_ENUM_VALUE returns HTTP 400, with an error response indicating the supplied type is not a valid enum value.

After CDC propagation, querying the consumer's org store filtered by type='department' returns the newly created org with all required fields (sourcedId, status, name, type, dateLastModified) intact and matching the publisher's record.

After CDC propagation, querying the consumer's org store filtered by type='district' returns orgA and does not return the newly created org (type='department'), confirming type-based isolation is consistent on the consumer side.

plans.title: PUT /orgs/{sourcedId} — existing org is replaced and propagates to consumer via CDC

setup.description: Ensure an org with a known sourcedId already exists in the publisher datastore (e.g., pre-created via POST /orgs) so that the PUT target is an existing record.
Record the current field values of the existing org (name, type, status, dateLastModified, etc.) so that post-PUT state can be compared against the replacement values.
Confirm the consumer service's CDC pipeline is active and subscribed to org change events from the publisher.

trigger.payloadShape: Full org replacement body containing all required fields: sourcedId (matching path param), name, status, type, dateLastModified (updated timestamp); optionally includes identifier, metadata, parent, children.

propagation.waitFor: Consumer has received and applied the CDC event for the updated org sourcedId.

assertions.assertion: HTTP response status is 200 OK.
The response body represents the replaced org and contains the sourcedId matching the path parameter.
The org's name, type, status, and dateLastModified in the response match exactly the values supplied in the PUT request body.

A subsequent GET /orgs/{sourcedId} on the publisher returns the org with the updated field values (name, type, status, dateLastModified) from the PUT body, confirming full replacement in the datastore.
The consumer's org record for the same sourcedId reflects the replaced values: name, type, status, and dateLastModified match those sent in the PUT request body.
No duplicate org entries exist for the same sourcedId on the consumer; only the single replaced record is present.

Fields not included in the PUT body (e.g., parent, children, metadata, identifier) are stored on the consumer exactly as provided in the replacement payload (absent or null if omitted), confirming full replacement semantics rather than partial merge.

plans.title: DELETE /orgs/{sourcedId} hard-deletes the org, returns 200 OK, and emits no CDC event to the consumer

setup.description: Ensure a valid org record exists on the publisher with a known sourcedId (e.g. pre-created via POST /orgs or seeded directly in DynamoDB), containing all required fields: sourcedId, name, status, type, dateLastModified.
Record the target org's sourcedId for use in the DELETE request and subsequent assertions.
Confirm the org is currently readable on the publisher by issuing GET /orgs/{sourcedId} and receiving a 200 response with the correct item.
Confirm the consumer's data store reflects the org's presence (e.g. it was previously synced via a prior CDC event) so absence after the delete can be meaningfully asserted.

Set up a CDC event monitor/listener on the SNS topic (or equivalent CDC propagation channel) to capture any events that arrive after the DELETE is triggered, for the duration of the propagation wait window.

trigger.payloadShape: No request body; the target org is identified solely by the {sourcedId} path parameter.

propagation.waitFor: Wait the full CDC propagation window (e.g. 30 seconds) to allow any potential DynamoDB Stream REMOVE record processing to complete and confirm no SNS publish occurs.

assertions.assertion: The DELETE /orgs/{sourcedId} response status code is exactly 200 OK.
After the DELETE, issuing GET /orgs/{sourcedId} on the publisher returns a 404 or empty result, confirming the org has been hard-deleted from DynamoDB and is no longer retrievable.
The org's sourcedId no longer appears in the 'items' array returned by GET /orgs on the publisher.

No CDC event (SNS message or equivalent) referencing the deleted org's sourcedId was received on the consumer during the propagation wait window — confirming that the DynamoDB Stream REMOVE record was NOT published to SNS per R-32.
The consumer's data store still contains whatever state it held for the org prior to the DELETE (i.e. it was not updated or removed via CDC), because no delete CDC event was propagated.

plans.title: Outbound ODCS Org Schema Validation: 500 on Non-Conforming Payload, Valid Payload Passes

setup.description: Ensure the publisher service is running and reachable at its live API base URL.
Ensure a CDC pipeline (change-data-capture) is configured between the publisher /orgs endpoint and the consumer service.

Pre-seed the publisher data store with at least one fully conforming org record containing all required ODCS fields: sourcedId, status, name, type, dateLastModified. Capture its sourcedId for use in assertions.
Confirm the consumer service is subscribed to org change events from the publisher and has a known endpoint or data store that can be queried to verify propagated org records.

Establish a test mechanism (e.g., a flag, mock, or fault-injection hook) on the publisher that can simulate an outbound serialisation failure — producing a representation that violates the ODCS org schema (e.g., missing a required field such as 'name') — for a designated org record, to validate the 500 error branch.

trigger.payloadShape: JSON object representing a new org with all required ODCS fields: sourcedId (string), status (string), name (string), type (string), dateLastModified (date), plus optional fields: identifier (string), children (array), metadata (object), parent (object)

propagation.waitFor: CDC event for the newly created org record has been consumed and processed by the consumer service, confirmed via polling or event acknowledgement

assertions.assertion: When POST /orgs is made with a fully conforming ODCS org payload, the publisher responds with HTTP 2xx (e.g., 201 Created) and the response body contains the org record nested under the 'items' array.

The org record returned in the 'items' array of the publisher response contains all required ODCS fields: sourcedId (string), status (string), name (string), type (string), and dateLastModified (date). No required field is absent or null.

The org record returned in the 'items' array conforms fully to the ODCS org contract schema: children is array (if present), identifier is string (if present), metadata is object (if present), parent is object (if present).

When the publisher's outbound serialisation is injected with a fault that causes the org representation to violate the ODCS org schema (e.g., missing required field 'name'), the publisher responds with HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.

When the publisher responds with HTTP 500 due to outbound validation failure, the response body does NOT contain a non-conforming org payload — i.e., the 'items' array is absent or empty, and no partial or malformed org object is returned.
After CDC propagation of the successfully created org, the consumer's data store contains an org record matching the sourcedId of the org created on the publisher.
The org record held by the consumer after CDC propagation contains all required ODCS fields (sourcedId, status, name, type, dateLastModified) with values matching those submitted to the publisher.

No org record corresponding to the fault-injected (schema-violating) org write attempt appears in the consumer's data store, confirming that the publisher's 500 response suppressed propagation of a non-conforming payload.

plans.title: Server-side dateLastModified is set on org create/update, ignoring any client-supplied value

setup.description: Record the current UTC timestamp (T_before) immediately before issuing the write request to the publisher.
Ensure no org with the test sourcedId exists on the publisher; if one does, delete it or use a unique sourcedId to guarantee a clean state.
Prepare a request payload that includes a deliberately incorrect/stale dateLastModified value (e.g. a date far in the past such as 2000-01-01) to confirm the server ignores it.

trigger.payloadShape: Object with required fields: sourcedId (unique string), status (string), name (string), type (string), dateLastModified (intentionally stale/incorrect UTC date string); optionally: identifier (string), children (array), parent (object), metadata (object)

propagation.waitFor: CDC pipeline delivers the newly created/updated org record to the consumer, confirmed when the consumer can retrieve the org by its sourcedId

assertions.assertion: The HTTP response status code is 2xx (201 Created or 200 OK).
The response body contains the org record with a dateLastModified field that is a valid UTC timestamp.
The dateLastModified value in the response is NOT equal to the client-supplied stale date (e.g. 2000-01-01); it must reflect the server-generated timestamp.

The dateLastModified value in the response is greater than or equal to T_before and less than or equal to T_after (timestamp recorded immediately after the request completes), confirming server set it to the current UTC time.
All other required fields (sourcedId, status, name, type) in the response match the values supplied in the request payload.

After CDC propagation, the consumer's copy of the org (retrieved by sourcedId) contains a dateLastModified field equal to the server-generated value observed in the publisher response, not the client-supplied stale date.
The consumer's org record contains all required fields (sourcedId, status, name, type, dateLastModified) with values consistent with those returned by the publisher.

If the same org is subsequently updated via PUT/PATCH on the publisher with another stale dateLastModified value, the consumer reflects the new server-generated dateLastModified (more recent than the first), confirming the behaviour holds for updates as well.

plans.title: Administrator user SHALL NOT appear on any class roster after CDC propagation of class write

setup.description: Ensure a user record exists with roles containing only 'administrator' (explicitly excluding 'student' and 'teacher') in the publisher system, with a known sourcedId.
Ensure the administrator user has been provisioned a login account in Cognito via the user-events → account-provisioning flow (R-24/R-55), confirming operator endpoint access is available.
Ensure at least one class record exists in the publisher with a valid sourcedId, classType, course, dateLastModified, school, status, terms, and title; this class will serve as the roster baseline.
Confirm no prior association exists between the administrator user and any class roster on the consumer side before the test trigger is fired.

trigger.payloadShape: Object containing required fields: sourcedId (string), classType (string), course (object), dateLastModified (date), school (object), status (string), terms (array), title (string); and optional fields: classCode (string), grades (array), location (string), metadata (object), subjects (array). The enrolled/associated user references, if any, must reference only users with 'student' or 'teacher' roles — the administrator user's sourcedId must NOT appear in any enrollment or membership associations within this payload.

propagation.waitFor: CDC event for the class entity emitted by the publisher is fully consumed and processed by the consumer service, updating the consumer's class roster data store.

assertions.assertion: GET /me/classes returns HTTP 200 with a response body containing an 'items' array; the class updated by the trigger is present in 'items' (matched by sourcedId), confirming CDC propagation succeeded.

None of the entries in the 'items' array returned by GET /me/classes are associated with the administrator user's sourcedId — the administrator does not appear as an enrolled member, student, or teacher on any class roster.
The class record present in GET /me/classes 'items' contains only user associations (if any) whose roles are 'student' or 'teacher', never 'administrator', confirming R-35 roster exclusivity.

The administrator user, when authenticating via the provisioned Cognito login account, receives access to operator endpoints (R-55) but a GET /me/classes for that administrator session returns an 'items' array that contains no roster entries attributing the administrator as a class participant.

plans.title: Org stored in DynamoDB with sourcedId as partition key propagates via CDC to consumer

Ensure the CDC pipeline (e.g., DynamoDB Streams + consumer listener) is active and healthy between the publisher and consumer.

propagation.waitFor: DynamoDB Streams event for the new org item to be processed and reflected on the consumer

assertions.assertion: After the POST to /orgs, the response status is 2xx and the returned org object contains a sourcedId matching the value submitted in the request payload.
A GET /orgs request returns a list under 'items' that includes the newly created org, with the correct sourcedId, name, status, type, and dateLastModified matching the submitted values.
The org record in DynamoDB can be retrieved using sourcedId as the partition key, confirming it is the primary key for the table (i.e., no duplicate or missing record when queried by sourcedId).
After CDC propagation completes, the consumer's representation of orgs includes the newly created org identified by the same sourcedId.

The org record on the consumer side has all required fields (sourcedId, name, status, type, dateLastModified) matching the values originally written by the publisher, confirming data fidelity through the CDC pipeline.
No duplicate org records exist on the consumer for the given sourcedId, confirming the partition key uniqueness constraint is respected end-to-end.

plans.title: GSI on `type` propagates org write and supports GET /orgs?type= query on consumer

setup.description: Ensure the publisher DynamoDB table has a Global Secondary Index (GSI) partitioned on the `type` field, as required by R-28.
Ensure the consumer service is subscribed to CDC events originating from the publisher org table.

plans.title: Integrity Validator: class.school Referential Constraint & classType/status Enum Validation via CDC Propagation

setup.description: Ensure the rostering store on the consumer is reachable and the integrity validator tooling is available and pointed at the consumer's rostering store.
Seed the publisher with a known valid org (school) record, capturing its sourcedId (e.g., knownOrgId).

Seed the publisher with a valid class record whose school.sourcedId references knownOrgId, classType is a valid enum value (e.g., 'scheduled'), status is a valid enum value (e.g., 'active'), and all required fields (sourcedId, title, course, dateLastModified, terms, school, classType, status) are populated.
Confirm the valid class has fully propagated to the consumer store via CDC before beginning the write trigger step.
Record the sourcedId of the valid class as baseClassId for reference in assertions.

trigger.payloadShape: Object containing all required class fields: sourcedId (string, unique), title (string), classType (valid enum string, e.g. 'scheduled'), status (valid enum string, e.g. 'active'), course (object with sourcedId), dateLastModified (ISO date string), terms (non-empty array of term references), school (object whose sourcedId intentionally references a NON-EXISTENT org to exercise the referential integrity failure path), and optionally classCode, grades, location, metadata, subjects.

propagation.waitFor: The newly created class record (identified by its sourcedId) is visible in the consumer store at GET /me/classes (present in the items array).

assertions.assertion: GET /me/classes returns an items array that contains the newly created class record, identified by its sourcedId — confirming CDC propagation completed.

Run the standalone integrity validator against the consumer rostering store. The validator MUST return a structured pass/fail report (e.g., JSON object or equivalent structured format), not plain text or an unstructured error message.

The structured report MUST contain at least one failure entry for the newly created class record, identifying the specific entity type as 'class', the specific sourcedId of the offending record, and the specific field 'school' as the failing referential constraint (school.sourcedId does not resolve to a known org in the store).
The structured report MUST NOT declare the overall store state as 'healthy' — the presence of the unresolved class.school reference is a hard stop for a healthy declaration.

The structured report for the previously seeded valid class (baseClassId) MUST NOT contain any failures — confirming the validator correctly distinguishes passing records from failing ones and reports only genuine violations.

If any additional class records exist in the consumer store whose classType value is not a recognized valid enum (e.g., not one of 'scheduled', 'homeroom', or equivalent contract-defined values), each such record MUST appear in the structured report with entity 'class', its specific sourcedId, and field 'classType' named as the failure.

If any additional class records exist in the consumer store whose status value is not a recognized valid enum (e.g., not one of 'active', 'tobedeleted', or equivalent contract-defined values), each such record MUST appear in the structured report with entity 'class', its specific sourcedId, and field 'status' named as the failure.

The structured report MUST enumerate every failure individually — multiple distinct violations across different records or fields must each appear as separate named entries, not collapsed or aggregated into a single generic error.
